extracted.intended_audience: scholars and researchers in humor studies, cognitive psychology, and related fields (those analyzing or designing jokes)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating or designing jokes using Forabosco's incongruity–resolution framework: identify incongruity, assess resolution, and judge cognitive effort and insight. Emphasizes interaction of cognitive domains and the conditions that make incongruity funny rather than merely confusing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception of incongruity (necessary but not sufficient)
rubrics_metrics.description: A stimulus is perceived as incongruous when it diverts from the cognitive model of reference. Perception of incongruity is necessary for humor but is not sufficient on its own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the joke produces a clear divergence from expectation or from the audience's cognitive model. Note that many incongruities do not produce laughter by themselves; presence of incongruity alone often leads to confusion rather than humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of resolution (or attempted resolution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolution (or an attempt at resolution) of the incongruity is a key factor: successful resolution reconciles or partially reconciles the domains that produced the incongruity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the audience can arrive at a reconciliation or at least a plausible partial reconciliation of the incongruity. Empirical finding: jokes that contain both incongruity and resolution are rated most humorous. Anti-pattern: incongruity without resolution typically yields confusion, not laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domains-interaction (two-domain interaction creating incongruity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The joke involves interaction between two cognitive domains; the interaction creates the incongruity and resolution attempts a partial reconciliation between those domains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze which cognitive domains are being bridged (e.g., literal/figurative, social/physical, professional/lay). Stronger, clearer domain interaction that produces a recognizable clash/reconciliation tends to support humor under this model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength of incongruity
rubrics_metrics.description: Stronger incongruity (a larger or more striking divergence from expectation) tends to make a joke funnier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the magnitude or salience of the divergence from expectation. However, strength must be balanced with resolvability — very strong incongruity that cannot be resolved may simply confuse the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleverness of the resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: The resolution should be clever — not obvious — and contribute to the humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the resolution shows a clever reinterpretation, unexpected link, or insightful twist. A clever resolution often increases amusement; overly obvious resolutions reduce funniness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution that opens new insight (illuminates something new)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolutions that illuminate a new perspective or insight make jokes funnier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the resolution yields an 'aha' that reveals a novel relation or observation the audience had not noticed. The Rubric explicitly asks: 'Does the resolution illuminate something new?'

rubrics_metrics.name: Modest, satisfying cognitive work required
rubrics_metrics.description: The resolution should require modest cognitive effort — enough to be satisfying but not so much as to be taxing or inaccessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the amount of mental work the audience must perform to reach the resolution. Forabosco emphasizes that resolution should require modest, satisfying cognitive work; if the effort is excessive, the joke may fail or produce frustration rather than amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience able to find/perform the resolution quickly
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience must be able to find (or perform) the resolution rapidly; quick performability correlates with greater humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the resolution path is discoverable by the intended audience in the time available (e.g., within a line or two). Forabosco lists 'resolution that audience can perform quickly' as a factor making jokes funnier, and the rubric asks, 'Is there a resolution path the audience can find?'

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of pure-resolution (no incongruity) or pure-incongruity (no resolution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither pure resolution without incongruity nor pure incongruity without resolution yields humor: pure resolution lacks the necessary incongruity, and pure incongruity produces confusion rather than laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a joke, ensure it contains both elements in balance. Use these anti-patterns as diagnostic checks: if a purported joke only resolves but never diverged from expectation, or only diverges with no resolvable reconciliation, it is unlikely to be humorous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall comedic quality judged by combination of dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor is best judged by considering the combination of incongruity strength, resolvability, cleverness, insight, and manageable cognitive effort rather than any single factor alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the rubric's questions collectively: Is there clear incongruity? Is there a findable and clever resolution? Does it require modest satisfying cognitive work? Does it illuminate something new? Use the combination as the primary evaluative heuristic rather than searching for a single decisive criterion. Also note Forabosco's caution that no single unified theory will capture all aspects of humor; multiple complementary perspectives may be helpful.
